deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a Latin draft, made in October 1851, of Riemann's formal petition to the Dean of the Göttingen philosophical faculty asking for admission to the doctorate. Under it are personal expense notes in German Kurrent with small sums.

(a) Salutation: 'Professor clarissime, Decane amplissime, Vir venerande'.

(b) Docket formula: 'A Decano clarissimo ordineque philosophorum amplissimo ea, qua par est, reverentia doctoris gradum petit G. F. B. Riemann, Breselenzensis, stud. math.'

(c) An abandoned opening: 'Quum adhuc physicis ac mathematicis operam dederim,'.

(d) A trial phrasing of the dissertation title: 'disquisitionem, quae in ponendis fundamentis theoriae generalis functionum complexae quantitatis variabilis collocata est'. This is the Latin rendering of 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'.

(e) The worked draft of the petition, with many corrections. In summary: having been a student of mathematics and physics, he asks the 'viri maxime venerandi' to create him doctor of philosophy on the basis of his knowledge of these arts. So that he may not seem unworthy of the honour, he sends a short vita together with the dissertation, which he ventures to submit to their judgement. It is dated 'Scripsi Gottingae die [?] mensis Octobris anni MDCCCLI'. The day is obscured by an ink blot. The next page has a revised version dated XXVIII[?] October.

(f) Accounts. The right-hand list reads: Milch bei Fischer 3 Ldr 16 1/2; Abendbrot 22; Mittagstisch 32 g. Then clothing items: Schneider; Rock; Sommerhose; Wäsche, Schnupftuch und schwarze Hose; Schuhe; 14 g. The left-hand column is a sum: 86 g + 22 g = 108 g, with '4 Ldr' written beside it. One possible reading, which is mine and uncertain: in the Hanoverian system 1 Taler = 24 gute Groschen, so 108 g = 4 Taler 12 g. However, the meaning of 'Ldr' (Louis d'or? Taler?) and how 86 was obtained are not clear from the page.
errors: No mathematical content to check. The one complete addition, 86 + 22 = 108, is correct.

The relation between the right-hand list (16 1/2 + 22 + 32 = 70 1/2) and the 86 in the left-hand sum is not evident. It may include further items or currency conversion; this cannot be resolved from the page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds a non-mathematical administrative draft and personal accounts. The facts of Riemann's 1851 doctoral application and dissertation are well documented. It has minor biographical interest only, such as student living costs and drafting of the Latin.

checkable.asserts: The left-hand column sum on the page is correct.
Milk, supper and lunch items total 70 1/2 (groschen), which is not equal to 86.
Under 1 Taler = 24 gute Groschen, 108 g = 4 Taler 12 g. This is a possible but uncertain link to the '4 Ldr' note.

transcription_corrections: 'Quum adhuc physices ad mathematicis operam dederim' should read 'Quum adhuc physicis ac mathematicis operam dederim'.
'Breslenzins[?]' is surely 'Breselenzensis' (native of Breselenz), matching the vita and the next page.

The date 'die 1 mensis Octobris' is uncertain. The image shows 'die' followed by a dot and an ink blot. The '1' seen near 'misi' is probably not a day number, so the day should be marked illegible. The next page's revision gives XXVIII[?].

In the corrected sentence the insertion above 'ne Vobis' looks more like 'ut digna sentio quam' relating to the struck phrase. The reading is uncertain, but the main text is 'Quo honore ne Vobis ... indignus videar/videri'.
'Abendbrot[?]' and 'Milch bei Fischer[?]' are plausible. 'Schneider' followed by 'Rechnung' (tailor's bill) is a likely reading of the next line.
